question: For a journey of 600 km, a truck covers the first 300 km at a speed of 42 km/hr. What speed (in km/hr) must it maintain for the remaining distance to achieve an average speed of 60 km/hr?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total time for avg 60 = 600 ÷ 60 = 10 hr

Time for first 300 km = 300 ÷ 42 = 50/7 hr

Remaining time = 10 − 50/7 = 20/7 hr

Speed for remaining = 300 ÷ (20/7)

**∴ Answer = 105 km/hr**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance = 600 km

First 300 km speed = 42 km/hr

Average speed = 60 km/hr

**Formula used:**

Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total time required = 600 ÷ 60 = 10 hr

⇒ Time for first 300 km = 300 ÷ 42 = 50/7 hr

⇒ Remaining time = 10 − 50/7 = 20/7 hr

⇒ Remaining distance = 300 km

⇒ Required speed = 300 ÷ (20/7)

⇒ = 300 × 7 ÷ 20

⇒ = 105 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 105 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed

Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time

Time Formula

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Remaining Concept

Remaining time = Total time − time already taken

Conversion Tip

Divide fractions carefully to avoid calculation mistakes
